title: नेपाली शब्दकोशको परम्परामा प्रज्ञा नेपाली बृहत् शब्दकोश {Nepali Dictionary Tradition in Prajya Nepali Brihat Shabda Kosh}
nepali: मानव जीवनको सम्पूर्ण क्रियाकलाप, चिन्तनमनन तथा अभिव्यक्तिहरूको सबैभन्दा सशक्त माध्यम भाषा हो । भाव तथा विचारको प्रस्फुटन एवम् सञ्चारका क्रममा भाषाले सामाजिक जीवनलाई गतिशील बनाउनुका साथै साहित्य तथा साहित्येतर ज्ञानविज्ञानको उचाइसम्म पु¥याउँने भाषाको अभिव्यक्ति क्षमता शब्दभण्डारको क्षमतामा निर्भर गर्छ । भाषामा भिजेका, खेलेका र रत्तिएका शब्दहरूकै समष्टि शब्दभण्डार हो । भाषाको सञ्चार सामथ्र्यको मापन गर्ने मूल आधार पनि शब्दभण्डार नै हो । शब्द सम्पन्नता र अर्थ वहन गर्ने क्षमताले भाषालाई जीवन्त तुल्याउँछ । शब्दकोश भाषाको शब्दभण्डारको सूचक भएकाले हरेक समृद्ध भाषामा शब्दकोश निर्माण गरिएका हुन्छन् । शब्दकोश भाषा सम्पन्नताको द्योतक पनि हो । आर. एल. टर्नरले नेपाली शब्द प्रविष्टि र अङ्ग्रेजी भाषामा अर्थ लेखिएको ‘नेपाली भाषाको तुलनात्मक तथा व्युत्पत्तिमूलक शब्दकोश’ सन् १९३१ मा प्रकाशन गरे । नेपाली भाषाको शब्दकोश लेख्ने पहिलो नेपाली विद्वान् पुष्कर शमशेर हुन् र उनको ‘अङ्ग्रेजी–नेपाली कोश’ प्रकाशित छ । चक्रपाणि चालिसेका ‘बगली कोश’ र ‘पर्यायवाची कोश’, हृदयचन्द्र सिंह प्रधानको ‘चिह्न परिचय’ र ‘शब्दशुद्धि विचार’, रामचन्द्र ढुङ्गानाको ‘नेपाली कोश’ आदिको प्रकाशनले नेपाली शब्दकोश निर्माणको पद्धति विकास हुँदै गयो । यसै परम्परामा वि.सं. २०१९ मा प्रकाशित बालचन्द्र शर्माको ‘नेपाली शब्दकोश’ को पृष्ठभूमिमा २०४० सालमा नेपाल राजकीय प्रज्ञा–प्रतिष्ठानबाट ‘नेपाली बृहत् शब्दकोश’ प्रकाशन भयो । यसपछि प्रकाशित नेपाली भाषामा ठुला आकारका अरू शब्दकोश वसन्तकुमार शम्र्मा नेपालको ‘नेपाली शब्दसागर’, आर.डी. प्रभास चटौतको ‘डोट्याली बृहत् शब्दकोश’, हेमाङ्गराज अधिकारी र बद्रीविशाल भट्टराईको ‘प्रयोगात्मक नेपाली शब्दकोश’, चूडामणि गौतमको ‘बृहत्तर नेपाली शब्दकोश’ र नेपाल प्रज्ञा–प्रतिष्ठानबाट प्रकाशित ‘प्रज्ञा नेपाली बृहत् शब्दकोश’ उल्लेखनीय छन् । यस अनुसन्धानात्मक लेखमा पुस्तकालयीय पद्धतिबाट हालसम्मकै बृहत् आकारमा रहेको ‘प्रज्ञा नेपाली बृहत् शब्दकोश’लाई प्राथमिक सामग्रीका रूपमा उपयोग गरिएको छ र कोशविज्ञानको सैद्धान्तिक पर्याधारमा {Language is the most powerful medium for human activities, expression of thoughts and deep contemplation. To make the social life dynamic, more expressive and meaningful, as well as to extend the horizon of literature and non- literary knowledge in its peak, the storage capability of vocabulary becomes the determinant factor. Lacking of it, lacks what is intended. Vocabulary itself examines communication skill. It is the integrated from of comprehended, played and used words. The efficiency and sufficiency of the word that carries the intended or denoted meaning makes the language alive. As dictionary is the indicator to show the storage of vocabulary, in each rich and rigorous languages dictionary are developed. R.L Turner published a comparative and etymological dictionary of the Nepali language in 1931 with Nepali word entries and English meanings. Puskar Shamsher is the first person who published Nepali- English dictionary. The publication of Chakrapani Chalise's 'Bagali Kosh' and Prayavachi Kosh, Hridaya Singh Pradhan's ‘Chinha Prichaya' and 'Shabdashuddi Bichar', Ramchandra Dhungana's ‘Nepali Kosh, etc., laid the milestones for the system of developing Nepali dictionary. Followed by the tradition mentioned above, and ‘Nepali Shabdakosh’ published by Balchandra Sharma in 2019, Nepal Royal Academy published ‘Nepali Brihat Sabdakosh in 2040 B.S. Then, the other remarkable dictionaries in Nepali language are: Basant Kumar Sharma's 'Nepali Shabdsagar', RD Chataut's 'Dotyali Comprehensive Dictionary', Hemangraj Adhikari and Badribishal Bhattarai's 'Prayogatmak Nepali Shabdakosh', Chudamani Gautam's 'Brihat Nepali Dictionary', and 'Pragy Nepali Brihat Shabdakosh' published by Nepal Academy. In this research article, 'Pragya -Nepali Brihat Shabdakosh ', which is the largest ever, has been used as primary source from the library. And its strong and weak aspects of this dictionary have been analyzed. Lastly, the conclusions have been drawn based on the theoretical framework}.
american_english:
Language is the most powerful medium of all the activity, thought and reflection, and expressions of human life.
In the course of the flowering and communication of feeling and thought, the expressive capacity of language, which makes social life dynamic as well as carrying it to the heights of literature and of non-literary knowledge and science, depends on the capacity of the vocabulary.
The vocabulary is the aggregate of the very words that have been steeped in the language, played in it and savored in it.
The basic basis for measuring a language's communicative capacity is the vocabulary itself as well.
Word wealth and the capacity to carry meaning make a language alive.
Because a dictionary is an indicator of a language's vocabulary, dictionaries have been produced in every rich language.
A dictionary is also a sign of a language's richness.
R. L. Turner published 'A Comparative and Etymological Dictionary of the Nepali Language', with Nepali word entries and meanings written in English, in 1931.
The first Nepali scholar to write a dictionary of the Nepali language is Pushkar Shamsher, and his 'English–Nepali Kosh' has been published.
With the publication of Chakrapani Chalise's 'Bagali Kosh' and 'Paryayavachi Kosh', Hridayachandra Singh Pradhan's 'Chinha Parichaya' and 'Shabdashuddhi Vichar', Ramchandra Dhungana's 'Nepali Kosh' and others, the method of Nepali dictionary-making kept developing.
In this same tradition, on the background of Balchandra Sharma's 'Nepali Shabdakosh' published in 2019 BS, 'Nepali Brihat Shabdakosh' was published by the Nepal Royal Academy in 2040 BS.
Other large-format dictionaries in Nepali published after this — Basanta Kumar Sharma Nepal's 'Nepali Shabdasagar', R. D. Prabhas Chataut's 'Dotyali Brihat Shabdakosh', Hemangraj Adhikari and Badri Bishal Bhattarai's 'Prayogatmak Nepali Shabdakosh', Chudamani Gautam's 'Brihattar Nepali Shabdakosh' and 'Pragya Nepali Brihat Shabdakosh' published by the Nepal Academy — are noteworthy.
In this research article, 'Pragya Nepali Brihat Shabdakosh', the largest in size to date, has been used as primary material through the library method, and, on the theoretical foundation of lexicography…
british_english:
Language is the most powerful medium of the whole of human life's activity, thought and reflection, and its expressions.
In the course of the bursting forth and communication of feeling and thought, the expressive capacity of language, which renders social life dynamic and likewise carries it to the heights of literature and of non-literary knowledge and learning, depends upon the capacity of the word-stock.
The word-stock is the aggregate of the very words that have been steeped in the language, played with in it and relished in it.
The fundamental yardstick by which a language's communicative capacity is measured is the word-stock itself as well.
Wealth of words and the capacity to bear meaning render a language vital.
Since a dictionary is an index of a language's word-stock, dictionaries have been compiled in every rich language.
A dictionary is a token of a language's richness as well.
R. L. Turner published 'A Comparative and Etymological Dictionary of the Nepali Language', with Nepali headwords and meanings given in English, in 1931.
The first Nepali scholar to compile a dictionary of the Nepali language is Pushkar Shamsher, and his 'English–Nepali Kosh' has been published.
The publication of Chakrapani Chalise's 'Bagali Kosh' and 'Paryayavachi Kosh', Hridayachandra Singh Pradhan's 'Chinha Parichaya' and 'Shabdashuddhi Vichar', Ramchandra Dhungana's 'Nepali Kosh' and the like saw the method of Nepali dictionary compilation steadily develop.
Within this very tradition, against the background of Balchandra Sharma's 'Nepali Shabdakosh', published in 2019 BS, 'Nepali Brihat Shabdakosh' was brought out by the Nepal Royal Academy in 2040 BS.
Among the other large-scale dictionaries in Nepali published thereafter, Basanta Kumar Sharma Nepal's 'Nepali Shabdasagar', R. D. Prabhas Chataut's 'Dotyali Brihat Shabdakosh', Hemangraj Adhikari and Badri Bishal Bhattarai's 'Prayogatmak Nepali Shabdakosh', Chudamani Gautam's 'Brihattar Nepali Shabdakosh' and 'Pragya Nepali Brihat Shabdakosh', published by the Nepal Academy, are worthy of note.
In this research article, 'Pragya Nepali Brihat Shabdakosh', the bulkiest to date, has been employed as primary material by the library method, and, upon the theoretical foundation of lexicography…
australian_english:
Language is the strongest medium there is for everything people do, think over and express in human life.
While feeling and thought are bursting out and being passed on, language gets social life moving and also lifts it right up to the heights of literature and of knowledge beyond literature, and how much a language can express comes down to how much vocabulary it has.
The vocabulary is the whole collection of the very words that have been dipped in the language, played around in it and taken delight in it.
The main measure of a language's communicative power is the vocabulary as well.
Plenty of words and the ability to carry meaning keep a language alive.
Since a dictionary shows a language's vocabulary, every rich language has had dictionaries put together in it.
A dictionary is a sign of a language's richness too.
R. L. Turner brought out 'A Comparative and Etymological Dictionary of the Nepali Language', with Nepali entries and the meanings written in English, in 1931.
Pushkar Shamsher is the first Nepali scholar to write a dictionary of the Nepali language, and his 'English–Nepali Kosh' is in print.
As Chakrapani Chalise's 'Bagali Kosh' and 'Paryayavachi Kosh', Hridayachandra Singh Pradhan's 'Chinha Parichaya' and 'Shabdashuddhi Vichar', Ramchandra Dhungana's 'Nepali Kosh' and others came out, the way Nepali dictionaries were put together kept improving.
Following that same tradition, with Balchandra Sharma's 'Nepali Shabdakosh', published in 2019 BS, as the backdrop, 'Nepali Brihat Shabdakosh' came out from the Nepal Royal Academy in 2040 BS.
Other big Nepali dictionaries published after that are worth a mention: Basanta Kumar Sharma Nepal's 'Nepali Shabdasagar', R. D. Prabhas Chataut's 'Dotyali Brihat Shabdakosh', Hemangraj Adhikari and Badri Bishal Bhattarai's 'Prayogatmak Nepali Shabdakosh', Chudamani Gautam's 'Brihattar Nepali Shabdakosh', and 'Pragya Nepali Brihat Shabdakosh', published by the Nepal Academy.
This research article uses 'Pragya Nepali Brihat Shabdakosh', the biggest one to date, as its primary material through the library method, and, on the theoretical groundwork of lexicography…

Book titles are kept as transliterations of the Devanagari. 'वि.सं. २०१९' and '२०४० साल' rendered as 2019 BS and 2040 BS; Turner's dictionary dated 1931 CE as in the source.
